message.content: In domestic cats and many other mammals, the presence of a mane (the long, shaggy fur around the neck and chest) is controlled by a dominant allele. In lions, the same principle applies: the allele that codes for a full mane is dominant over the allele that codes for a short or absent mane. Thus, if a lion inherits one copy of the “mane” allele from either parent, it will develop a full mane. This makes the mane a classic example of a dominant genetic trait in lions.
